The Harrods beauty advent calendar for 2026 has been unveiled, and we are in for a treat this December. Comprising 34 products (two more than last year) and 21 full-size items (a whopping seven more than 2025), the department store is delivering something considerably bigger and better than we’ve seen previously.

This year’s advent haul is a true representation of the retailer’s expansion into beauty (it launched H Beauty – its dedicated beauty locations outside of London – in 2020) and its luxury heritage. You can expect to unbox formulas from the likes of La Prairie, Augustinus Bader and Sisley.

Whether you’re swatting up on all of 2026’s calendars so far in a bid to find the very best, or you’re a true Harrods devotee, here’s everything you need to know before the retailer’s Christmas countdown launches next month. Plus, browse details on the separate hair and body, and fragrance advent calendars, which, in 2025, sold out in record time.



Harrods beauty advent calendar 2026 True to form, the Harrods beauty advent calendar for 2026 is a luxury offering. While the calendar still leans heavily into the high-end skincare synonymous with the department store's beauty halls, newer additions from Skin Cycles, U Beauty and Sync Beauty sit comfortably alongside heavyweights such as Augustinus Bader, Sisley and Shiseido. For anyone who buys a beauty advent calendar to sample products they'd never usually justify splurging on, Harrods remains one of the strongest contenders. There's a 15ml pot of Augustinus Bader's the rich eye cream, Shiseido's future solution LX cream and a Montale fragrance – all of which, if bought outright in the featured sizes, would cost more (£273) than the entire advent calendar. The category split also feels expertly curated. Make-up products from the likes of Charlotte Tilbury, Gucci Beauty and Nars feature alongside haircare from Philip Kingsley and Moncho Moreno. The numbers are more impressive this year, too. The price has increased by £20 to £270, but Harrods has added two extra products overall and boosted the full-size count from 14 to 21. As always, I'd treat that figure with a little caution until every product size is confirmed, as luxury retailers have a habit of stretching the definition of “full-size”. News.content:

Unknown American Jackson Suber was the surprise leader of the Open at Royal Birkdale but it was compatriot Bryson DeChambeau making waves on and off the course.

By the time the 26-year-old world number 115 had signed for a five-under 65, DeChambeau had left his mark on the links and six-time major winner Sir Nick Faldo with a sarcastic response to claims he had “zero clue on strategy”.

A fast and fiery Birkdale burned Masters champion Rory McIlroy who, as a late afternoon starter, got the more difficult wind and crusty greens and missed at least three putts from inside four feet in a round of 72 which left him seven off the lead.

Two-time major winner DeChambeau is searching for his first Claret Jug but after shooting his first sub-70 major round of the year he took aim at Faldo.

On Tuesday the last English winner of the Open, in 1992, criticised the 32-year-old’s approach.

“I’d say it to his face: he has zero clue of strategy. He said it last year, I think, ‘I’m going to go out and attack the links’. Well, I’ve never ‘attacked’ a links,” said the three-time Open champion.

DeChambeau, looking to avoid missing the cut in all four majors this year, refused to speak to the media for the fifth consecutive major round but spoke to the R&A’s in-house channel.

In one 18-second response he used the word ‘strategic’ or ‘strategy’ three times, pointedly stressing the emphasis.

“I think you’ve got to be a lot more strategic out on the golf course. I feel like I did a really good job today of being incredibly strategic and focused super hard on placing it in the right places,” he said after a 67 left him two off the lead.

“Besides 18, I placed the ball in some good areas. I just need to hit more fairways. Other than that, I feel like my strategy was nice today.”

McIlroy salvaged something from his round with a brilliant 198-yard approach at the last to five feet to finally sink a short birdie putt.

It still left the Northern Irishman with plenty to do if he wants to win a second Claret Jug and a seventh major to officially become the most successful European golfer of all time, as each of the last 26 Open champions have been within five of the top after round one.

“If you look at the discrepancy between the scoring this morning and this afternoon, it looks like that’s going to be flipped tomorrow with the conditions again,” said McIlroy, who won his first Masters last year after a seven-shot first-round deficit.

“Hopefully I can take advantage of the more benign conditions in the morning and get back in it.”

Suber carded six birdies and an eagle to sit one ahead of Yorkshireman Dan Brown and South Korea’s Sungae Im.

Brown is hoping his chances do not go up in smoke after getting through almost half a packet of cigarettes to cope with the stress.

Asked whether there had been any request not to light up on the tinder-dry course the 31-year-old, who carded a 65 on his major debut at Troon in 2024, said: “I’ve haven’t been told otherwise, but I’ve been making sure they’re out.

“I’m probably on seven or eight a round; stress levels go up, then probably the more I end up having.”

open image in gallery Dan Brown jointly leads the first round of The Open for the second time in three years (Peter Byrne/PA) ( PA Wire )

Scotland’s Bob MacIntyre sat alongside DeChambeau in a group which also included 2018 champion Francesco Molinari.

Defending champion and world number one Scottie Scheffler, at two under, said: “Any time you can shoot under par to start a major championship, it’s a good spot to be in.”

News.title: Brilliant Root picks off India to set up decider
News.content:
India immediately summoned back Bumrah with England 37 short of their target but Root, head down, nursed his side home to set up a series decider at Lord’s on Sunday. He was partnered well by Atkinson who capped a decent performance with the ball with a bright 23, even lifting Burmah for six.

Root is enjoying a rebirth in ODI cricket. He has averaged over 80 for the past 18 months and his career average is back above 50 for the first time in four years. The fact the 50 over format closely resembles Test cricket now is making a batsman of Root’s class priceless and with a Test captaincy job vacant at the moment this will have done his chances no harm at all.

He even managed to shake off the kryptonite of the keeper standing up. It is the in vogue way to bowl to England with Hawkeye showing under two percent of balls in international cricket last summer were bowled with the keeper up to the stumps - this season it is closer to 15 percent. Root just took it in his stride this time although the tactic did not suit India’s tall seamers in the same way it did New Zealand recently.

Batting time has been England’s problem. Root’s younger team-mates struggle with longer innings and it is not necessarily their fault because they play so little 50 over cricket before being picked by England.

Root grew up with the format and 40 over county cricket too which many of the 2019 World Cup winners acknowledged helped them hone their aggressive game for ODIs.

The current generation live on a diet of T20 and because of Hundred commitments cannot play in the county one day cup. Jacob Bethell is opening and not looked comfortable so far. He was out half playing a shot as if caught in two minds whether to have a crack or leave it. In Test cricket he plays a simple game, relies on his strengths and is a good leaver. In T20 he smacks it. This format requires some kind of balance. It will take time but he will crack it.

News.title: McIlroy leaks bogeys as putter goes cold in first round at the Open
News.content:
A stone-cold putter cost an erratic Rory McIlroy on a frustrating first day at The Open as a two-over round of 72 left him seven off the lead and already facing an uphill battle.

The Masters champion was unfortunate in that he went out at 3.15pm in the most difficult conditions of a day which began somewhat benign with no wind.

By the time he finished at 8.43pm the greens, baked in the harsh sun all day, were at their crustiest and that may possibly explain why he missed three putts from inside four feet and was 104th in the putting statistics.

He was literally brought to his knees at the par-five 17th where, after hooking his approach into the gallery and then flying the green into a bunker, he contorted his stance to splash out to eight feet – only to miss for a sixth bogey.

He at least finished on a positive with a brilliant approach from 198 yards to five feet and finally sank a short birdie putt.

But the distance to unknown American leader Jackson Suber meant his bid for a second Claret Jug and a seventh major – which would officially make him the most successful European golfer of all time – was dealt an early blow.

Each of the last 26 Open champions have been within five of the lead after round one.

The morning starters benefited from a mere whiff coming out of the east but the world number two went out with the breeze stiffening and moving to a more northerly direction off the sea.

As a result, McIlroy found himself two over after seven having failed to get up and down at the par-three fourth and two-putted from inside four feet at the short but tricky seventh.

He missed a three-footer at the next – this time for birdie – but finally got one to drop after driving the green at the downwind, 415-yard ninth to turn in one over.

Back-to-back bogeys at the start of his back nine halted any momentum as he dropped as low as 155th out of 156 in the putting statistics.

At the 13th a 24-footer dropped into the side of the hole, encouraged by a sardonic tilt of the head from McIlroy, who was seemingly unimpressed by his second birdie of the day.

However, he made a complete mess of the two par-fives – having holed a 12ft birdie at the 206-yard 15th – but salvaged something late on.

News.title: ‘I feel like I’m in front of a fireball’: 45C heat becomes India’s new normal
News.content:
Even under the shade of an umbrella, the fierce heat is unbearable. It’s nearing midday as Gulab Padiyar hammers yet another metal sheet into a simple bucket, but temperatures topped 40C hours ago.

“I feel like I’m in front of a gas stove – or a fireball,” Ms Padiyar says, perched on a once-white cushion beside a dusty road. “I feel like I’m cooking myself.”

The 53-year-old has little choice: it’s heat or hunger. Each day, Ms Padiyar earns around 400 rupees (roughly £3) making dozens of buckets – it’s just enough for her and her husband to survive.

“I feel dizzy and my eyes burn, sometimes I get headaches or faint,” she says. “But at the end of the day… this is the work I know, and others won’t employ me because of my age. So I think I have to continue, no matter how hot it gets.”

Ms Padiyar’s hometown, Ahmedabad, is no stranger to scorching temperatures. Home to roughly 8.5 million people, it’s the largest city in Gujarat – an arid state in western India where both Mahatma Gandhi and Narendra Modi, the country’s Prime Minister, were born.

But the mercury is rising. In the 1990s, the hot season between mid-March and mid-June averaged roughly 35 days above 40C, according to analysis from The Times of India. This year, that number hit 71. A study from the University of Oxford this month ranked Ahmedabad as the world’s second most “heat-risk city”, after Basra in Iraq.

Yet the Indian city has also been a trailblazer in extreme heat policy. Its experiences in the last 15 years offer strategies to adapt – and a warning about just how difficult that is, especially to protect workers in a “survival economy”.

News.title: Pound hits one-year high on hopes of Chancellor Mahmood
News.content:
The pound has hit a one-year high on hopes that Shabana Mahmood will be named Andy Burnham’s chancellor.

Sterling climbed 0.6pc against the euro to tip above €1.18, its highest level since June last year, after the Home Secretary emerged as the frontrunner to replace Rachel Reeves. Over the same timeframe, the pound rose as much as 0.8pc versus the dollar to more than $1.35.

Ms Mahmood is thought to be in pole position to take over from Rachel Reeves at the Treasury when Mr Burnham enters Downing Street on Monday, after weeks of speculation about his Cabinet choices.

Mr Miliband, the Energy Secretary, had previously been considered the top contender for No 11 after advising Mr Burnham, who won the Makerfield by-election last month, on his economic plans.

However, he is viewed less favourably by markets over concerns he will pursue a more Left-leaning agenda than rivals.

Philip Shaw, chief UK economist at Investec, said the pound had performed strongly against the euro and dollar as reports that Ms Mahmood was the frontrunner to become the next Chancellor were “soothing market fears of unduly lax fiscal policy”.

The rally for the pound also came as Britain’s economy returned to growth in May in a boost for incoming prime minister Andy Burnham.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 0.1pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

It marked a rebound from a 0.1pc decline in April, which had been the first contraction in eight months.

Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics said the economy has been “more resilient” than previously thought but warned higher fuel prices would still restrain real incomes.

He said the 0.1pc rise in UK GDP in May “is not a bad welcome gift for incoming prime minister Andy Burnham”.

News.title: At the moment of reckoning, England’s old anxiety took hold
News.content:
All the years that have passed since those red shirts on a summer’s day at a long-gone Wembley Stadium – the humiliations, the occasional triumph, the plentiful servings of self-pity. For a short while in Atlanta it felt like that epoch might finally be ending and all it came down to was managing the last five minutes and whatever the beleaguered referee might add.

A place at a World Cup final was within England’s grasp, a mere 60 years since the last. But just as it loomed into view, already the players and their manager were tracing an old path. The man currently in charge of the England team might be German, the players might be of a generation finessed under bold new coaching ideas, but once more a familiar anxiety took hold. England were minutes from the prize. Yet team and manager were already obeying an old instinct to sabotage the moment.

England had been in retreat long before Lionel Messi served up for Enzo Fernández the goal that would level this World Cup semi-final, and then the second for Lautaro Martínez ,which would propel Argentina forward. Of course, Messi is Messi, and this Argentina team exist to exert his will on games by any means necessary. Yet, as ever, at the moment of reckoning, England demonstrated all the resistance of damp cardboard.

Thomas Tuchel once again reverted to the deep defensive position. Once again, the adapted five-man back line sat on the edge of their area. Against Mexico in the last 16, Tuchel was dismissive of any suggestion he had invited pressure, asking what other option he had with just 10 men. Against Norway in the quarter-finals he did the same, once Erling Haaland was off the pitch. Against Argentina, a team accustomed to playing with it all on the line, such a move was fatal.

Sports.title: Heartbroken Harry Kane left ‘empty’ and moans at ‘missing piece of puzzle’ as he breaks silence on England World Cup KO
Sports.content:
HARRY KANE has broken his silence on England’s World Cup semi-final elimination.

The Three Lions had one hand on a spot in the final after going 1-0 up against Argentina, but threw it away after shrinking into old defensive habits that allowed Lionel Messi to pop up with two assists to turn the tie on its head.

But captain Kane, who scored six goals in the tournament, has now taken to social media to express his feelings on yet another summer of heartbreak for England.



Writing on Instagram, he said: “No words are big enough right now to overcome this empty feeling in the stomach.



“We were close, really close to another final but it wasn’t enough. We’ve given everything over these last seven weeks and to fall short is hard to take!

“I know the expectations are high and rightly so, we’ve been knocking on the door for eight years now but again are missing that final piece of the jigsaw!”

With Kane at the helm, England have made two World Cup semi-finals, a quarter finals and made two European Championship finals but lost both.



But he continued: “That’s where we have to go away, process it and find a way to get better.

“I’m so proud of the boys and what we have shown throughout this tournament – some tough games and tough environments that we have overcome.

“Some memories that will stay with us players and I’m sure you fans for a long long time! Going for glory doesn’t always mean you will get it.

“You have to fight for it, get knocked down, pick yourself up and go again and that’s what we will do, there’s no other way but to keep believing and keeping pushing.”



Kane concluded: “Thank you to every single fan that travelled and showed their support in the stadiums.

“Thank you to every fan back home for believing in us.

“Thank you to the boys and staff for everything you have given.

“As always, win or lose, we learn and go again!”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel facing FA probe into England’s World Cup exit and rollercoaster campaign including TV row with Bellingham
Sports.content:
THE inquest into England’s World Cup exit is set to continue with The FA set to launch a probe into the Three Lions’ rollercoaster tournament.

Thomas Tuchel‘s side were eliminated at the semi-final stage as they fell to a 2-1 defeat to Argentina.



Naturally, disappointment has been immense as the fallout of that elimination continues.

But according to The Times, the FA are now set to launch a full inquest looking at the tournament as a whole, before providing an assessment on the performance of the manager.



Tuchel retains the full support of the FA, and FA chief Mark Bullingham is understood to want to honour Tuchel’s full contract which runs until 2028.

England had a topsy-turvy World Cup, which had seen equipment robbed before they had even played their opener against Croatia.



They went on to win that game, albeit with a dodgy defensive display to boot, before clean sheets followed against Ghana and Panama, but saw the goals dry up as England struggled to break down low blocks.

The same could be said for the DR Congo clash, who took a shock lead before Harry Kane‘s brace got England out of trouble and set up a last 16 game with Mexico at the Azteca.

That match was arguably the highlight of the tournament in terms of performance, with England coming through with a narrow win despite being down to 10 men for most of the second half.

Next came Norway, with England coming from behind to win in Extra Time.

But the flashpoint of that game came after the final whistle, with Tuchel slamming the England display as “sloppy” in an interview with ITV before that was put to match-winner Jude Bellingham, who didn’t take too kindly to the criticism.

Captain Kane went on to accuse the broadcaster of trying to stoke division in the camp before England played Argentina – their biggest World Cup game since the semi-final against Germany in 1990.

However, England were initially undaunted by the reigning world champions and took a 1-0 lead through Anthony Gordon.

But old habits proved to die hard as England became passive and invited pressure onto themselves when it really mattered, with the situation ultimately not helped by Tuchel’s perceived negative subs.

The Times report states FA Insiders are sympathetic to Tuchel over the criticism he is receiving, as at no point did he instruct the team to withdraw into their own half after taking the lead.



Reports had said players were unhappy with the defensive display they had shown and had seemingly directed those feelings toward the manager, but FA sources insisted those feelings were actually directed at themselves.

Tuchel himself had suggested it was not in England’s “DNA” to keep the ball like it was with the likes of Spain or Argentina, and that had ultimately been a factor in them losing control of the game.

Ultimately, Lionel Messi popped up with two assists that condemned England to a third-place play-off against France, while they face Spain for a shot at football‘s ultimate prize in the final.

Sports.title: Euro 2028 tickets – when are tickets available, and how much will they cost?
Sports.content:
ENGLAND fans are hurting after the Three Lions’ World Cup semi-final exit.

But the football calendar moves quickly, and attention is already turning to the next major tournament.

Euro 2028 is coming to the UK and Ireland, bringing the elite of European football straight to our doorstep.



But as any seasoned match-goer knows, the real battle begins long before kickoff – it starts at the ticket office.



Following widespread fury over astronomical pricing at the 2026 World Cup, UEFA has promised a different approach for the Euros.

When are Euro 2028 tickets on sale?

UEFA has confirmed that tickets will only go on sale after the final tournament draw has taken place in December 2027.

Previously, fans had to apply blindly for match tickets before they even knew which teams would be playing where.

This time, supporters will know exactly who is playing, which stadium they will be at, and what dates to book off work before they part with their hard-earned cash.

UEFA is set to announce full details of the ticketing phases and allocations in Autumn 2027.

The general public sale is expected to open shortly after the December draw.

How much will they cost?

UEFA is taking a stand against soaring ticket inflation, and has confirmed a “broad freeze” on ticket prices, keeping core costs locked at Euro 2024 levels.



It has pledged that at least 1.2 million tickets – over 40% of the total ticket allocation across the UK and Ireland – will be priced in the two most affordable categories.

That means you’ll be able to secure a group-stage ticket for just £26 (€30), while the next tier up (Category 3) will be capped at around £52 (€60).

To keep things fair, UEFA has also banned “dynamic pricing,” meaning ticket prices will remain flat from start to finish.

Will there be a ticket ballot?

To ensure a fair distribution of tickets, the general public sales phase will operate via a randomly allocated ballot system.

This means there’ll be no need to sit in online queues refreshing your screen; everyone who applies within the designated application window will have an equal chance of being selected.



UEFA has also confirmed that over 80% of all available tickets will go directly to the general public and fans of the participating teams.

To combat touts and ticket scalping, an official resale platform will also be set up.

Fans who can no longer attend will be able to sell their tickets safely at face value, with no hidden fees for the seller.

Sports.title: ‘Not in our DNA’ – Thomas Tuchel in shock verdict over England’s collapse as World Cup trophy drought rages on
Sports.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL claims England were not good enough at the World Cup – although the German is set to keep his job despite the disastrous World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina.

Fans and pundits have attacked Tuchel for his negative tactics after England threw away a 1-0 lead to lose 2-1 in Atlanta.



Tuchel, now preparing for a third place play-off against France in Miami on Saturday, says his team must improve if they are to win anything.

He said: “I still feel there is an extra level that we need to conquer and need to step up to the next level to get the big prize.



“I loved every day. I said after the Norway game that I see a disconnect from what I see in training on a football level and within the games. I think we can impose ourselves more on the ball.

“I still think we can show how good football players we are. I think that is still in us, as I see it in training and in every camp. And here also at the World Cup.

“As always you need a bit of time to digest, to reflect and to analyse. It just takes time and you have to bounce back. That is what sport demands. High level sports demand that of us. That’s basically the next step.”

Although there have been calls for the sack, the FA are planning to stick with Tuchel having given him a new two-year contract. He will be in charge for when England co-host the Euros in two years.

He said: “I’m very pleased and I enjoyed every single day and I enjoyed every single minute of the first 55 minutes of the semi-final. We just couldn’t cope with the momentum swing.

“I think ball possession plays a crucial role. It’s maybe not in our DNA like it is in the Spanish DNA or Argentinian or Brazilian DNA. To take the ball, control the game and the ball which is also a big problem.”

Pressed on whether he definitely wants to stay in charge, he added: “Yes, 100 per cent. There is still enough to improve, and I am more than happy to do that.”

FA chief executive Mark Bullingham said: “It is heartbreaking to be so close. The players and Thomas gave it everything today and the squad, coaches and staff could not have worked harder during the tournament.

“I would like to thank them all – and also give my heartfelt thanks to our wonderful fans here in the USA and at home. We felt your support every step of the way and we are all so disappointed not to go further.”

Tuchel will make mass change for the game against the French with the fringe players likely to start.

Sports.title: England players shocked by Thomas Tuchel’s bizarre retreat in disastrous World Cup exit but boss set to keep his job
Sports.content:
ENGLAND players were left shocked by Thomas Tuchel’s bizarre World Cup retreat that arguably cost the Three Lions a place in the final.

Tuchel‘s side were leading 1-0 against Argentina as late as the 84th minute, but fell to a 2-1 defeat after Lionel Messi popped up with two assists to break English hearts.



The ex-Chelsea manager was accused of making “cowardly” subs when bringing on extra defenders in place of wingers and attackers.

However, the 52-year-old claimed the subs were made to try and help the players close the gaps in the defence, with Argentina ramping up the pressure and missing a number of chances before getting their reward.



Tuchel also insisted he had “no regrets”, but according to The Telegraph, the changes he made to bring on Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn and Nico O’Reilly stunned some players.

The report claims there was belief in the squad that the reigning world champions were there for the taking after Anthony Gordon‘s opener.

Ollie Watkins, Bukayo Saka, and Noni Madueke were left on the bench while Ivan Toney and Marcus Rashford only came on in the 96th minute.

There is also a belief that replacing Declan Rice with a midfielder instead of an attacker inadvertently engineered Enzo Fernandez’s equaliser when Messi dropped it to the edge of the area before the Chelsea star’s long-range strike.

Marc Guehi said of the performance: “Once we went 1-0 up we seemed to just try and hold on, which at this level is just not enough, so I’m gutted.

“We should have carried on. We should have carried on pushing. It kind of felt like we scored and then the mentality was go back, defend.”

Speaking to the BBC after the game, Tuchel had said he and his coaching staff had changed nothing after Gordon’s goal, but said the game changed completely.

He had said after the game: “Millions of coaches after the game think that they know better. I have to make a decision, it’s how I analysed the game.

“No regrets. The team gave everything and played one of our better matches, probably our best under the circumstances.”

England continues to be gripped by a fearful mindset when it comes to the big games, which was reflected in yet another painful exit.

Tuchel was brought in to change that mentality, but one non-playing source told The Telegraph: “Tuchel was brought in for his knockout tournament tactics and he got it wrong.”



Meanwhile, another added: “Nobody could understand it.”

The report adds that despite the disappointment and ignominy of a third-place play-off against France this Saturday, rather than a first final since 1966, Tuchel retains the backing of The FA.

FA Chief Mark Bullingham is said to want to honour Tuchel’s full contract that runs until the next European Championship in 2028.

That would give Tuchel two more years to potentially change the mentality of the English national team to be one that does not wilt in key moments, with the Euros being played on British soil.

Sports.title: Will Argentina players be suspended for the World Cup final after raising controversial Falklands banner?
Sports.content:
ARGENTINA broke English hearts after beating the Three Lions 2-1 in Wednesday night’s World Cup semi-final – but the victory has been overshadowed by a controversial banner.

Anthony Gordon’s strike left England fans believing this could be the year that 60 years of pain comes to an end.

But Enzo Fernandez’s brilliant strike, followed by a stoppage-time header from Lautaro Martinez, saw the reigning champions book their second consecutive World Cup final spot.



And after the final whistle, grinning players, including Manchester United’s defender Lisandro Martinez, paraded a banner across the field.



It declared “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, referring to the British-administered Falkland Islands.

Now this incident is expected to trigger an investigation from Fifa, which could see players miss out on the showpiece match against Spain.

Will Argentina players be suspended for the World Cup final?

Fifa has not announced whether any players could be suspended just yet, leaving uncertainty over whether the incident will have consequences beyond a potential fine.

While Fifa’s sanctions will likely target the Argentine FA rather than individual stars, the fallout could still be felt in the Premier League when the 2026/27 season kicks off.

Several members of the Argentine squad – including Lisandro Martinez (Manchester United), Enzo Fernandez (Chelsea), Cristian Romero (Tottenham), and Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool) – play in England.

But these players are unlikely to face domestic bans from the FA, as the incident occurred under FIFA’s jurisdiction at an international tournament.

Why was the Falklands banner controversial?

The Falkland Islands remain a sensitive subject, and the 1982 conflict between Britain and Argentina cost the lives of 255 British servicemen and 649 Argentine personnel.



The islands remained under British control following the 74-day war.

But by parading the slogan in front of a global audience immediately after defeating England, the Argentine team re-opened historical wounds on the pitch.

Fifa has strict rules designed to keep geopolitics out of football.

World football’s governing body bans “banners, flags, flyers, apparel and other paraphernalia that are of a political, offensive, and/or discriminatory nature” inside match venues.

Displaying political messages during or immediately after a match is a breach of these regulations, which exist to ensure football remains neutral.



What could Argentina’s punishment be?

Fifa has said it is “assessing match reports” under “standard procedure” – but has not yet commented on whether a formal investigation will be launched.

England fans hoping for a dramatic reinstatement to Sunday’s final against Spain will be disappointed.

Under Fifa’s disciplinary code, political gestures of this nature almost always result in financial penalties rather than sporting sanctions.

The most likely outcome is a hefty fine for the AFA, perhaps exceeding the £20,000 handed out in 2014, alongside a formal warning about future conduct.

Fifa does hold the power to impose points deductions or event bans for extreme or repeated rule breaches, but there’s virtually zero chance that Argentina will be disqualified from Sunday’s final at MetLife Stadium.



While a ban from the World Cup final is unlikely, international governing bodies have previously suspended players for making sovereignty claims after defeating England.

Has anything like this happened in previous tournaments?

This is not the first time the Argentine Football Association (AFA) has landed itself in hot water over this exact banner.

In 2014, ahead of the World Cup in Brazil, Argentine players displayed the same “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” sign before a friendly match against Slovenia.

Fifa quickly opened disciplinary proceedings and slapped the AFA with a £20,000 fine for violating rules on team misconduct and “preventing political messages”.

In addition to this, during Spain’s trophy celebrations, the pair took to the stage in front of thousands of fans and led chants of “Gibraltar es Español” (“Gibraltar is Spanish”).



Gibraltar has been a British Overseas Territory since the 18th century.

Uefa’s disciplinary panel ruled that Rodri and Morata had violated the “basic rules of decent conduct” and used a sporting event for “manifestations of a non-sporting nature”.

Both players were forced to serve a one-match suspension during a Nations League match against Serbia.

Sports.title: Falklands ‘hope’ Fifa sanction Argentina as islanders hit out over ‘insensitive’ banner & say they’re ‘not surprised’
Sports.content:
The Falkland Islands have slammed Argentina for its “insensitive” post-match banner and called on Fifa to sanction the shameless squad.

Lionel Messi and Co sparked fury when they waved a vulgar sign saying “The Falklands are Argentinian” after beating The Three Lions 2-1.



The British Overseas Territory said: “The Falklands government is disappointed – though regrettably not surprised – that the Argentine football team decided to tarnish the result of last night’s World Cup football semi-final – a game that did not in any case involve the Falkland Islands.

“That said, it is hardly news to anyone that the people of the Islands were victims of an aggressive invasion in 1982, which left many traumatised.



“The banner displayed by Argentina last night, therefore, was particularly insensitive for many people in the Falklands.”

They added: “It is the avowed policy of the Falkland Islands Government that we do not wish to see politics being brought into sport.



“Nor do we wish the Islands and their people to be used as a political football in every conversation about England and Argentina.”

The Islanders also welcomed Downing Street’s supportive statement this morning over their sovereignty.



They then called on Fifa to “make good on their promise to keep politics out of sport” and sanction the disgusting display.

Argentina’s shameless players are even trying to wriggle out of sanctions by pointing the finger at their own players.

When quizzed on the vile display, spineless defender Gonzalo Montiel claimed: “They just threw one down from the stands and the boys grabbed it.”



Argentina’s madcap president has even backed up the team and boasted that they’ll probably only receive a fine for their pathetic behaviour.

Nationalist firebrand Javier Milei spewed: “It is perfectly valid and legitimate for the players to want to express themselves and do so.”

Prior to kick-off, Argentina fans had been warned not to enter Atlanta Stadium with flags containing any reference to the Falklands.

The country’s National Security Minister Alejandra Monteoliva confirmed it would be considered “political content”.

She said: “Argentine or English flags are permitted, but nothing that contains any message that could provoke any kind of incident.



“It will not be possible to enter with bottles or with any item that contains a provocative message: political, hateful, or promoting racial or religious intolerance.”

However, when later quizzed about the restrictions, U-turning Monteoliva said: “You can’t ban a chant or silence people.”

Downing Street has since backed calls for Argentina to be hit with some form of punishment from Fifa for the abhorrent display.

A statement from No10 on the controversy read: “The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are.”

Cabinet minister Peter Kyle said it was “entirely inappropriate” for this to happen in the aftermath of Argentina’s comeback victory.



Reform leader Nigel Farage said: “Whilst I am disgusted at the behaviour of some Argentinian players last night, the most important thing to do is build up the Royal Navy quickly.”

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch added: “The Falkland Islands are British. The Conservatives will always defend them.”

Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey also took to social media to say: “In August 2024 Rodri and Álvaro Morata were rightly banned for one match for singing ‘Gibraltar is Spain.’

“Now the Argentine players who celebrated with the ‘Falklands are Argentine’ banner must be barred from the final.”

Under Fifa’s disciplinary code, political gestures of this nature usually result in financial penalties rather than sporting sanctions.



The Argentine Football Association (AFA) will most likely face a hefty fine, alongside a formal warning about future conduct.

This comes after Argentina furiously protested a Royal Navy warship sailing through its waters near the Falkland Islands.

Buenos Aires lodged a seething complaint after HMS Medway, an offshore patrol ship, sailed to and from the Antarctic.

London insisted the voyage complied with maritime law and the Argentinian government was warned long in advance.

The Falkland Islands is a British Overseas Territory in the south-west Atlantic Ocean 300 miles off Argentina’s east coast.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Britain has had control of the islands since winning a bitter war to defend them from Buenos Aires in 1982, after Argentina invaded and occupied the territory.

The conflict claimed the lives of 255 UK servicemen, three islanders, and 649 Argentine personnel.

Sports.title: England players shocked by Thomas Tuchel’s bizarre retreat in disastrous World Cup exit but boss set to keep his job
Sports.content:
ENGLAND players were left shocked by Thomas Tuchel’s bizarre World Cup retreat that arguably cost the Three Lions a place in the final.

Tuchel‘s side were leading 1-0 against Argentina as late as the 84th minute, but fell to a 2-1 defeat after Lionel Messi popped up with two assists to break English hearts.



The ex-Chelsea manager was accused of making “cowardly” subs when bringing on extra defenders in place of wingers and attackers.

However, the 52-year-old claimed the subs were made to try and help the players close the gaps in the defence, with Argentina ramping up the pressure and missing a number of chances before getting their reward.



Tuchel also insisted he had “no regrets”, but according to The Telegraph, the changes he made to bring on Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn and Nico O’Reilly stunned some players.

The report claims there was belief in the squad that the reigning world champions were there for the taking after Anthony Gordon‘s opener.

Ollie Watkins, Bukayo Saka, and Noni Madueke were left on the bench while Ivan Toney and Marcus Rashford only came on in the 96th minute.

There is also a belief that replacing Declan Rice with a midfielder instead of an attacker inadvertently engineered Enzo Fernandez’s equaliser when Messi dropped it to the edge of the area before the Chelsea star’s long-range strike.

Marc Guehi said of the performance: “Once we went 1-0 up we seemed to just try and hold on, which at this level is just not enough, so I’m gutted.

“We should have carried on. We should have carried on pushing. It kind of felt like we scored and then the mentality was go back, defend.”



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Speaking to the BBC after the game, Tuchel had said he and his coaching staff had changed nothing after Gordon’s goal, but said the game changed completely.

He had said after the game: “Millions of coaches after the game think that they know better. I have to make a decision, it’s how I analysed the game.

“No regrets. The team gave everything and played one of our better matches, probably our best under the circumstances.”

England continues to be gripped by a fearful mindset when it comes to the big games, which was reflected in yet another painful exit.

Tuchel was brought in to try and change that mentality, but one non-playing source told The Telegraph: “Tuchel was brought in for his knockout tournament tactics and he got it wrong.



Meanwhile, another added: “Nobody could understand it.”

The report adds that despite the disappointment and ignominy of a third-place play-off against France this Saturday, rather than a first final since 1966, Tuchel retains the backing of The FA.

FA Chief Mark Bullingham is said to want to honour Tuchel’s full contract that runs until the next European Championship in 2028.

That would give Tuchel two more years to potentially change the mentality of the English national team to be one that does not wilt in key moments, with the Euros being played on British soil.

Sports.title: England LIVE reaction: FIFA response to Falklands banner, Kane breaks silence, Tuchel sack calls

England's hopes of World Cup glory were extinguished, with FIFA forced to respond after Argentina players unfurled a political banner about the Falkland Islands in the aftermath

England's World Cup hopes are over after they fell short against reigning champions Argentina in Atlanta on Wednesday night.

Thomas Tuchel's men led 1-0 with five minutes of normal time remaining thanks to Anthony Gordon's goal, but defensive changes and an inability to keep possession proved crucial as a stunning Enzo Fernandez effort and an injury time header from substitute Lautaro Martinez sent Lionel Messi and co into another final.

On a night where both national anthems were booed by opposing supporters and Argentina players celebrated post-match with a flag that declared 'The Falklands belong to Argentina' England stars were left gutted by their failure to reach Sunday's final against Spain.

It was a night where Tuchel's substitutions badly backfired and a number of key men were NOT at their best, with Wayne Rooney pointing the finger of blame squarely at the Three Lions boss.

Despite calls for him to vacate his post, Tuchel has vowed to continue with England for the remainder of his contract - which will see him through until Euro 2028. He said: "We keep on going with the contract until the home Euros. I'm looking forward to that even though right now it's difficult to look that far ahead."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel facing FA inquest despite under-fire England boss' Euro 2028 vow
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel facing FA inquest despite under-fire England boss' Euro 2028 vow

Thomas Tuchel has come under heavy fire for what many perceive to be negative tactics as England fell to a late World Cup semi-final defeat against old foes Argentina

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel has been heavily criticised following England's exit from the World Cup (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

The Football Association will conduct a thorough review of Thomas Tuchel's performance at the World Cup as well as England's campaign in full once the dust has settled following a painful defeat to Argentina.

‌



Tuchel has been heavily criticised by fans and pundits alike over the manner of England's heartbreaking 2-1 loss, with a tandem of quickfire Argentina goals denying the Three Lions what would have been a first World Cup final appearance since 1966. Anthony Gordon had given England the lead, but Lionel Messi seized control shortly after and orchestrated a rousing comeback as Tuchel's side dropped.

‌



As Argentina prepare for a second successive World Cup final, England and Tuchel have been left to lick their wounds ahead of Saturday's third-place play-off against France.

‌



And while reports have indicated The FA are firmly behind Tuchel despite the backlash over how England wilted in the second half, The Times report that they will conduct a review of his performance as well as that of the team.

FIFA respond to 'insensitive' Argentina banner as Falkland Islands Government speaks out READ MORE :

John McDermott and a technical department will lead the review, with the report adding that it remains to be seen whether Tuchel will retain the same level of support once all aspects of the tournament have been assessed.

While Tuchel led England to what is just the fourth World Cup semi-final in their history and oversaw what many perceive to be the finest away performance in history courtesy of a rousing victory against Mexico at The Azteca, performances were often scrutinised.

‌



View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel and England were beaten by Argentina in Atlanta (Image: AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

The German signed a two-year contract extension to take him through to Euro 2028 in the months leading up to the World Cup. Mark Bullingham, The FA's chief executive, later revealed there was a performance-related clause in said agreement.

Wayne Rooney was among the pundits to point the finger of blame squarely at Tuchel after the match with the overwhelming feeling being that England retreated too deep, too early.

‌



But when Tuchel was asked if he was still the man to lead England into Euro 2028, his response was defiant.

View 3 Images England were leading before having their hearts broken late on (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

“Yes, 100 percent. There is still enough to improve, and I am more than happy to do that.

‌



“I’ve loved it here. I loved every day. I said after the Norway game that I see a disconnect from what I see in training on a football level and within the games I think we can impose ourselves more on the ball. I still think we can show how good football players we are. I think that is still in us, as I see it in training and in every camp. And here also at the World Cup.

“I still feel there is an extra level that we need to conquer and need to step up to the next level to get the big prize.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel makes Euro 2028 vow as under-fire England boss doubles down on tactics
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel makes Euro 2028 vow as under-fire England boss doubles down on tactics

Thomas Tuchel insists he should lead England into the next tournament, which is a home Euros, as he's forced to defend the tactics that cost them a World Cup final spot

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel is adamant he remains the right man for England going forward

Thomas Tuchel insists he is “100 percent” the manager to take England forward. He has two years left on his £5m-a-year contract but is facing a huge backlash after England’s defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final.

‌



England boss Tuchel oversaw a memorable campaign which got them into the last four but they blew a glorious chance to reach the final for the first time in 60 years.

‌



Former England captain Wayne Rooney led the criticism by slamming Tuchel’s substitutions and insisting his tactics were too negative and handed victory to Argentina.

‌



When asked whether he is the man to take England forward into Euro 2028, Tuchel said: “Yes, 100 percent. There is still enough to improve, and I am more than happy to do that.

Should Thomas Tuchel stay on as England boss? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

Thomas Tuchel bottled it and FAILED his players - but FA must take portion of blame READ MORE :

“I’ve loved it here. I loved every day. I said after the Norway game that I see a disconnect from what I see in training on a football level and within the games I think we can impose ourselves more on the ball. I still think we can show how good football players we are. I think that is still in us, as I see it in training and in every camp. And here also at the World Cup. I still feel there is an extra level that we need to conquer and need to step up to the next level to get the big prize.”

Tuchel now faces the unenviable task of facing France in the third place play-off in Miami on Saturday which comes less than 72 hours after their heartbreaking defeat to bitter rivals Argentina.

‌



England are likely to make wholesale changes while Tuchel also plans to use the rest of the summer to reflect upon the World Cup campaign and also the reasons why they could not go one step further.

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel's changes ultimately curtailed the team's hopes

Tuchel believes a huge part of the reason why England ran out of steam at the end was too many players joined up nursing knocks after a tough season with their clubs.

‌



Tuchel added: “As always you need a bit of time to digest, to reflect and to analyse. It just takes time and you have to bounce back. That is what sport demands. High level sports demands that of us. That’s basically the next step. We struggled physically as well, through the whole tournament playing in the heat, playing in the altitude, playing with a man down and so on. It cost us a lot in the end. We gave everything but it was not enough.”

Tuchel has also defended his tactics against Argentina - but admitted they just could not live with Lionel Messi. Tuchel insisted his plan would have worked but said his players sat too deep, they were too passive and also claimed no team could have kept out Messi and Co.

‌



He said: “There were two wide wingers suddenly. Two very wide wingers that they didn’t have before and two strikers in teh middle and started to cross. So we went to a back five to be closer to the wingers, to not let them have 20 metres to them, but maybe only 10 and be more aggressive.

“Still he had three centre-backs as we struggled to defend the crosses before. I thought if they start crossing now with Messi we will not close every left foot of Messi. Crosses will always come in so we will have three central defenders. And of course like in every structure it was important to stay active and push out and step out and fight duels. We just couldn’t.

“I think in this moment my feeling is that no structure in the world could have helped us because we were too passive. We were not physical enough, we didn’t stop runs arriving in our box and the deliveries were then too good.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel caught the England disease he was so critical of during World Cup collapse
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel caught the England disease he was so critical of during World Cup collapse

Thomas Tuchel's decision to go defensive was an England habit we've seen for years on end, despite the German supposedly being the man to bring a tournament edge when it counted

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel allowed England to fall back in bad habits (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel was brought in to solve England’s failings - not confirm them. Sadly, Tuchel, amid the painful fall-out of another World Cup disappointment, was back talking about England’s age-old problem of not being able to keep the ball.

‌



Back in March, Tuchel said former boss Gareth Southgate’s team were “afraid” to lose in Euro 2024 rather than “having the excitement and hunger to win it.”

‌



Fast forward four months and it felt as if Tuchel himself has caught the English disease because his side looked most in danger of defeat after taking the lead.

‌



Tuchel talked about the players being “passive”, insisting they were told to step up and not being able to keep the ball. Basically, it felt like the manager was putting the blame at the players’ door. It actually felt as if it had been Tuchel who had gone defensive as soon as England went ahead and was ready to sit and defend the lead.

Thomas Tuchel makes Euro 2028 vow as underfire England boss doubles down on tactics READ MORE :

England boss Tuchel said: “If then it happens then it has to be changed. But I’m not sure, I always try to think in football terms, in football matters. I haven’t seen the data yet but I think right after the goal, the momentum swings completely in ball possession, chances and it drops dramatically.

“I think ball possession plays a crucial role. It’s maybe not in our DNA like it is in the Spanish DNA or Argentinian or Brazilian DNA. To take the ball, control the game and the ball which is also a big problem.

‌



“We got too passive within our structure. I tried to help, not too become more passive with a back five in our structure but to be more active, to be quicker out to the wingers, not to open up the gaps between the back four. We encouraged everyone to step out, to be more active within the structure but we just struggled.

“But we also played against a lot of quality, urgency, quality and there was one offensive player after another. They were strong on the ball, they got stronger and stronger in the first contacts in the technical execution they were at the highest level.

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel had criticised Gareth Southgate for not being brave enough in games (Image: Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty Images)

‌



“We couldn’t fight any duels any more which was why we dropped deeper and deeper which was never the plan but it happened. Couldn’t stop the runners from second line, the midfielders through our lines and the deliveries were on the highest level. We needed to get back on the ball otherwise you cannot break the pressure and you cannot get the momentum back.”

Surely it is Tuchel’s job to take away the fear, to improve England’s quality in possession and also get the tactics spot on. That was why Tuchel was brought in: to be the experienced, top level winning manager to help get England over the line after so many near-misses in tournaments.

Instead, England played like they did under Southgate when they surrendered a lead in the 2018 World Cup semi final or in the Euros in 2021.

‌



The data which Tuchel had not seen in the aftermath of defeat makes depressing reading. They had 12 per cent possession - yes, 12 - between taking the lead against Argentina and conceding the winner in stoppage time.

To say England had lost control of the game, might be the understatement of the year. That has to be on Tuchel just as it was on Southgate in the past. England needed a leader on the sidelines and all they got was a tactician who tried to shut up shop against Lionel Messi and Co. That must go down as a huge mistake because you cannot protect a lead for so long against such quality.

‌



That is the reason why England missed out on the World Cup final. They said goodbye to Southgate, brought in a well-paid, high-profile manager - and ultimately he did just the same as the last guy. Tuchel did defend his tactics, insisting he was happy with his players and similar efforts against Mexico in the last 16 when they finished as heroes.

Tuchel added: “Very pleased with them, I’m very pleased and I enjoyed every single day and I enjoyed every single minute of the first 55 of the Argentina game. Because I think we were there, ready to go for it, not be passive and actually go for it and try. We just could’d cope with the momentum swing.

“You can also defend. You can also defend deep. You can stay active. We did this for example in Mexico and did this in matches. It can happen that you can get deep but you have to stay active and we struggled.”

Sports.title: Cesc Fabregas tells England's Thomas Tuchel exactly what he would NEVER do as manager
Sports.content:
Cesc Fabregas tells England's Thomas Tuchel exactly what he would NEVER do as manager

England boss Thomas Tuchel has been widely criticised for his defensive changes in the 2-1 World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel has been criticised for his defensive changes in England's World Cup semi-final defeat (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

World Cup winner, turned manager, Cesc Fabregas, has previously explained why he wouldn’t take the same approach as Thomas Tuchel during a game. The England boss has come under heavy criticism for his approach to the closing stages of the World Cup semi-final vs Argentina.

‌



England had taken the lead through Anthony Gordon in the 55th minute. But they quickly found themselves under pressure as Argentina searched for the equaliser.

‌



In response, Tuchel made defensive changes to his team, in the 72nd minute, defender Ezri Konsa replaced goalscorer Gordon. 10 minutes later, Dan Burn replaced Reece James and Nico O’Reilly came on for Declan Rice as England looked to see out the game as they did in the previous rounds against Mexico and Norway.

‌



This time, the tactic didn’t pay off, with Enzo Fernandez scoring for Argentina with five minutes of normal time left to play. They completed the turnaround through Lautaro Martinez in the second minute of added time.

England stars' reaction to controversial Thomas Tuchel tactics vs Argentina revealed READ MORE :

FIFA respond to 'insensitive' Argentina banner as Falkland Islands Government speaks out READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The decision to bring defensive players onto the pitch, ahead of the likes of Marcus Rashford or Bukayo Saka, for the final 18 minutes has drawn a lot of criticism from fans and pundits alike. It seems that Fabregas, who won the World Cup with Spain in 2010, and is now the manager of Italian Serie A side Como, would also disagree with the decision.

‌



In a previous interview shared on social media, Fabregas said: “Like if you are winning 1-0, for example, and you change a midfielder or a striker, and you put a defender in the last 10-15 minutes, you’re playing with a back five all of a sudden.

“Because you saw from outside that they are playing with really high fullbacks, or whatever reason. Inside the players, you see that he’s taken a striker off, he’s put a defensive player on.

“So automatically, your mindset is, ‘oh, the coach wants us to defend, we have to sit back’. You attract pressure, and you invite them to have the ball more, and you invite them to attack you more and to be more dangerous, and the more they are on your pitch.

‌



View 2 Images England manager Thomas Tuchel came under fire for his changes in the World Cup semi-final (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

“Yeah, one day it can happen, that you can kill them on counterattack and score the second goal, but 80, 90 per cent of the time it backfires because you invite pressure and there’s a penalty, there’s a little free kick or cross, rebound.”

The Telegraph reports that members of the England squad were left ‘shocked’ by the defensive changes and the approach to the game.

‌



Former England captain Wayne Rooney is in agreement. Speaking after the match, he said: "You can't go a goal up and then surrender, surrender the ball and surrender any opportunity of trying to get the second goal. You want to be on the front foot when the pressure is on Argentina to get back in the game."

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

He added: "If you're on that pitch, go 1-0 up and then see the changes the manager is making…you are losing belief. There's only so many times you can get away with it. You start thinking 'We're going to sit back, how are we going to get through this?'"

Article continues below

Tuchel, himself has said that he has ‘no regrets’ over the decision. Speaking on BBC after the match, he said: “Millions of coaches after the game think that they know better. I have to make a decision, it’s how I analysed the game.

"No regrets. The team gave everything and played one of our better matches, probably our best under the circumstances.”

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola gets major boost as 'future Liverpool captain' agrees new contract
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola gets major boost as 'future Liverpool captain' agrees new contract

Liverpool's new manager, Andoni Iraola, is preparing to oversee his first season at Anfield and will welcome the news that one of their best players is set to sign a new contract

View 2 Images Dominik Szoboszlai is set to sign a new contract (Image: Getty Images)

Dominik Szoboszlai is understood to be on the cusp of committing his future to the club after reaching an agreement in principle on a new contract.

‌



The news will come as a significant boost to Liverpool's new manager, Andoni Iraola, who was named as Arne Slot's successor last month. Szoboszlai was one if not Liverpool's most consistent performers during a challenging 2025-26 campaign which culminated in Slot losing his job after overseeing a fifth place finish, even filling in at right-back on occasions.

‌



Szoboszlai had two years remaining on his current deal heading into the summer but speculation over his long-term future had been growing as a result of his stellar form, while the player himself conceded that talks had stalled back in April.

‌



It now seems as though Szoboszlai will be staying at Anfield for the foreseeable future, though, with The Guardian confirming contract terms have been provisionally agreed.

Liverpool confirm Jeremy Jacquet shirt number as new transfer seizes on major exit READ MORE :

Not only will such news be welcomed by Iraola as he prepares to take charge of his maiden campaign, it will be well received among other figures: including club legend Steven Gerrard, who has made it clear he is a big fan of Szoboszlai.

The Hungary captain's swashbuckling, all-action style of play and penchant for a spectacular goal has already seen him likened to one of Liverpool's all-time great players. And Gerrard even predicted earlier this year that Szoboszlai would go on to follow in his footsteps by donning the captain's armband in the future.

‌



"I like his mentality," Gerrard told TNT Sports back in March. "He's evolved, and he's grown a lot since he's become a Liverpool player.

View 2 Images Steven Gerrard has already identified Dominik Szoboszlai as a future Liverpool captain (Image: Franco Arland, Getty Images)

"We obviously signed a big talent. He's in the prime years of his career. I think Liverpool are going to see the best of him.

‌



"I hope he stays around for a long time because I think there's a potential captain in there. The way he's playing and his consistency and his mentality, you can hear it in his voice.

"He's straight on to the next game, talking about Brighton. I love that about him. He's flying at the moment. He's full of confidence. He's got everything going for him. He's just got to maintain it and stay healthy."

Sports.title: FIFA respond to 'insensitive' Argentina banner as Falkland Islands Government speaks out
Sports.content:
FIFA respond to 'insensitive' Argentina banner as Falkland Islands Government speaks out

The Falkland Islands Government wrote to FIFA expressing their 'disappointment' after Argentina's players unfurled an 'insensitive' banner after beating England in the World Cup semi-finals

View 2 Images Argentina's players held a banner which translated to 'The Falklands are Argentine' (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

FIFA are investigating after Argentina's players displayed what the Falkland Islands Government described as an 'insensitive' banner following their win against England. A late comeback in Atlanta saw Argentina snatch a 2-1 victory, sending them through to the World Cup final.

‌



During the full-time celebrations, a group of Argentina players held up a banner which read: "Las Malvinas son Argentinas (The Falklands are Argentine)." It comes after Argentina's players sung a chant referencing the Falklands in the wake of their 3-2 victory over Egypt in the round of 16.

‌



The banner has sparked backlash from the UK, with many believing that it was offensive to the 255 British soldiers who were killed during the Falklands War in 1982. A statement from the UK Government issued on Thursday morning reiterated: "The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are."

‌



Ed Davey, leader of the Liberal Democrats, even called for any players who celebrated with the banner to be 'barred from' Sunday's final against Spain. The Falkland Islands Government has also written to football's global governing body.

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

England miss out on £18m payday immediately after Argentina heartbreak READ MORE :

England World Cup player ratings: Bellingham shines but Arsenal duo suffer after gruelling season READ MORE :

FIFA responded to the backlash by saying: "As is standard procedure, FIFA's independent Disciplinary Committee is currently assessing the match reports and considering the relevant circumstances before deciding on potential further steps."

‌



The aforementioned letter read: "The Falkland Islands Government is disappointed - though regrettably not surprised - that the Argentine football team decided to tarnish the result of last night’s World Cup football semi-final - a game that did not in any case involve the Falkland Islands.

"That said, it is hardly news to anyone that the people of the Islands were victims of an aggressive invasion in 1982 which left many traumatised. The banner displayed by Argentina last night, therefore, was particularly insensitive for many people in the Falklands.

View 2 Images The banner has sparked backlash from the UK and Falkland Islands (Image: Jewel SAMAD/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"It is the avowed policy of the Falkland Islands Government that we do not wish to see politics being brought into sport. Nor do we wish the Islands and their people to be used as a political football in every conversation about England and Argentina.

"We welcome the UK Government's supportive statement this morning. As Business Secretary Peter Kyle highlighted, the World Cup has as one of its central tenets that politics is separate from football. We hope FIFA will make good on their promise to keep politics out of sport, and sanction all behaviour of this nature in line with its own rules."

Sports.title: Serrano to fight Argentina's Manzur for world titles in TikTok first
Sports.content:
Amanda Serrano will put her world titles on the line against Lucrecia Manzur in California on August 21 in a landmark fight being shown on TikTok.

The Puerto Rican star defends her WBA and WBO featherweight world titles against Argentine Manzur in the first-ever unified women's world championship contested over 12 two-minute rounds, promoted by MVP.

After a barnstorming second-round stoppage victory over Cheyenne Hanson at the end of May for her 32nd professional KO, Serrano returns to the ring aiming to break the all-time women's knockout record.

The fight, being staged at Pechanga Resort Casino in Temecula, will also be the first championship boxing event broadcasted live on TikTok.

"I've dedicated my career to creating opportunities for women's boxing and bringing our sport to the biggest stages possible, so to headline the first-ever championship boxing event on TikTok is incredibly meaningful," said Serrano.

"Women's boxing deserves to be seen by as many people around the world as possible, and this partnership gives us the chance to introduce our sport to a massive global audience in a completely new way.

"I'm also proud that Lucrecia and I will be making history in the first-ever unified women's world championship contested over 12 two-minute rounds. Every time I step into the ring,

"I'm fighting for Puerto Rico, and on Friday August 21, I have the opportunity to make history for my island, break the all-time women's knockout record, and defend my world titles. This will be a night to remember for Temecula and boxing fans around the world."

Image: Amanda Serrano is a multi-weight world champion

Manzur is the WBO's No 2 contender with a 14-4 career record featuring seven knockouts.

"I've been asking for this opportunity for a very long time," said Manzur.

"Ever since I started boxing, I've dreamed of fighting for a world title, and now I have the chance to do it against one of the sport's true icons and someone I've always admired - Amanda Serrano.

"I have tremendous respect for everything Amanda has accomplished and for the legacy she has built. But once we step into the ring, my focus is on winning."

The stacked MVP card also includes US Olympian Jahmal Harvey against Hammet Keb in a six-round lightweight bout, and Brazil's Jully Poca against the USA's Cinderella Linnear in a four-round super lightweight bout.

Image: Most Valuable Promotions have hailed Amanda Serrano as the 'Most Accomplished Female Fighter Ever'

"From day one, MVP has challenged the traditional boxing model by creating the biggest moments and opportunities for fighters while finding new ways to bring the sport to fans around the world," said Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions.

"Partnering with TikTok to deliver the first-ever championship boxing event on TikTok LIVE is another example of that vision to grow the audience for boxing and make world championship fights more accessible than ever. This event will also further activate MVP's loyal fanbase among hard-to-reach Gen Z and Gen Alpha audiences, demographics that MVP has consistently reached better than anyone else in the sport.

"This would not be possible without the MAFFE, the Most Accomplished Female Fighter Ever, Amanda Serrano. Sports.title: Britain's Bearman 'flattered' by Red Bull rumours amid Verstappen uncertainty
Sports.content:
British driver Oliver Bearman says he is "flattered" by speculation linking him to Red Bull amid ongoing uncertainty over Max Verstappen's future with the team.

Verstappen has a Red Bull contract until 2028 but his representatives are understood to have held talks with McLaren in the last month as the four-time world champion weighs up his options for next year.

Since then, Haas' Bearman has been rumoured to be of potential interest to Red Bull in the future, and the British driver was asked about the links ahead of this weekend's Belgian Grand Prix, live on Sky Sports F1.

"It's quite flattering to hear things like that, to with a team like Red Bull, who are incredibly successful and to be connected with them in any way, even if it's just rumours is very nice," said Bearman, who is midway through his second full F1 campaign.

"But like I said, it's just rumours, and I'm fully focused on what I'm doing here with Haas at the moment."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the best moments from Oliver Bearman’s 2024 debut race weekend for Ferrari when he stole the show finishing in a brilliant seventh place

Bearman has been a Ferrari junior since 2022 and made his debut at the 2024 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix for the Scuderia as a replacement for Carlos Sainz, who underwent surgery for appendicitis.

He made his full F1 debut last year for Haas but had the upper hand on team-mate Esteban Ocon, a trend which has continued this season.

The 21-year-old, who does not have a contract for 2027, has previously stated his "ultimate target" is a future Ferrari seat and would rather be at Ferrari over Red Bull, if given the choice but is "waiting in the dark".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Bearman is reduced to tears after driving Ayrton Senna's 1985 Lotus 97T, the car Senna drove to his first-ever Formula 1 victory

"I don't have a full, let's say, say in in that. But Ferrari have trusted me from the very beginning in Formula 3 and put me in that car in 2024 as well," he said.

"They are really the reason that I'm here right now. At the moment I'm enjoying what I'm doing with Haas and the faster I can go now, the easier I make my life in the future."

Verstappen tight lipped over future

As for Verstappen, he is understood to have until October to decide whether he wants to stay at Red Bull for 2027.

The Dutchman is free to activate a clause in his contract which would allow him to leave at the end of this season as he will not be top two in the Drivers' Championship after the Hungarian Grand Prix, the last round before the summer break.

"I don't want to go here and say yes and no, and this and that, about my future. I've said already many times that if there was something new, I would say it myself," said Verstappen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive Max Verstappen's troublesome 2026 season, with the Red Bull driver having suffered multiple issues in the opening nine races

The main factor in Verstappen's decision will be performance and Red Bull have endured a mixed season so far as they continue to recover from a disappointing start to the year.

Despite making their own power unit for the first time, Red Bull were deemed to have the best engine by the FIA, but have been lacking performance in the corners due to aerodynamic and chassis deficiencies.

But, Verstappen was within two seconds of victory only two races ago at the Austrian Grand Prix, before he spun out due to a rear wing failure at the British Grand Prix - the second active aero-related problem, which led to a crash, in two weeks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show, Jenson Button suggests Max Verstappen should look to leave Red Bull sooner rather than later

"We're just looking to the future, trying to fix the current issues that we have on the car, but that's a very open discussion," said Verstappen.

"Sometimes you get a little bit disappointed or upset after a race, but, for example, after Silverstone you go home, you reset. On Wednesday, I was back at the factory and then you prepare again for the weekends ahead. That's how we've been operating all the years together.

"Of course, some years you're just a little bit more competitive than others, but in terms of my approach and how we work as a team, nothing really changes."

Sports.title: Hamilton: Mercedes should be a lot further ahead in title battle
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says Mercedes pair Kimi Antonelli and George Russell "should be a lot further ahead" of him than they are in the Drivers' Championship.

Antonelli leads Russell by 25 points at the top of the standings with Ferrari's Hamilton just seven points further back than his former team-mate.

Mercedes have clearly had the fastest car for much of the season but have been hit by reliability issues, which along with a few other factors have allowed Hamilton to remain in striking distance as the season approaches its halfway stage.

Ahead of a final double-header before the summer break gets under way in Belgium this weekend, Hamilton was asked about the relative tightness of the standings.

The seven-time world champion said: "I mean, I don't really look at it much. I don't think about it. I don't think it's particularly relevant.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton claims Sprint Pole at the British Grand Prix!

"I mean, it's great that we're all close when really Mercedes have been the strongest team and they should be a lot further ahead.

"So, that's exciting for the rest of the year, hopefully."

While Antonelli and Russell have each failed to score points at two grands prix, Hamilton has yet to finish outside the top six and has picked up four podiums in his last five races, including a first victory for Ferrari in Barcelona.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix

Strong reliability has also enabled Ferrari to stay in touch with Mercedes in the Constructors' Championship, which the Silver Arrows lead by 78 points.

Asked whether Ferrari's reliability could prove to be the difference in the battle for titles, Hamilton added: "I hope so. Often in championships, that is the case.

"And that's really down to the amazing work the team's done in really building us a reliable car.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton enjoyed his short break before the Belgian Grand Prix as he took to the waves with Kim Kardashian

"That's no easy feat, to build a fast and reliable car, so I'm very grateful to them for that.

"And then, just trying my best to extract everything in every single lap, and every single point I can out in the car."

Hamilton 'gutted' for England after World Cup exit

Hamilton had been showing support for England's football team throughout the World Cup on social media, and admitted he was "gutted" after watching their heartbreaking defeat to Argentina on Wednesday.

Asked by Sky Sports F1 if he could give the nation a boost by winning at Spa-Francorchamps this weekend, Hamilton replied: "I think it will be tough this weekend, but, yeah, I watched in pain last night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Formula One's British drivers share how they feel following England's World Cup semi-final exit

"So proud of the boys for getting us as far as they did. I can imagine how much work they put in, how much time and effort, and, of course, they had all the support, but, yeah, tough against Argentina.

"Oh, my God. And I just felt gutted for them. Sitting there with my fingers, everything crossed, hoping that we would pull it off, but we'll bounce back.

"And in terms of us (Ferrari) this weekend, I really have no idea. I mean, I come here to try and win, that's for sure."
